newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All newspapers
FORMER MINISTER GETS 10 YEARS IMPRISONMENT

Kalpnath Rai, food minister in the previous Congress party government headed by Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, was sentenced to 10 years in prison on charges of sheltering six people wanted by police. Rao had been convicted of harbouring members of an alleged underworld gang believed to be linked to a string of bomb blasts in Bombay in March 1993 that killed 260 people. He was also fined one million rupees ($27,932). Rai, who has denied the charges, said he would appeal against the order in a higher court.
The Hindustan Times
DELHI BUDGET HIKES PETROL, LIQUOR PRICES

The Delhi government's budget for 1997/98 (April-March) pushed up prices of petrol, petroleum products, diesel, liquor and cement. The budget, presented by the state finance minister, hiked sales tax rates on these items. The increase on sales tax on conventional vehicle fuels comes at a time when there was speculation of the federal government increasing petrol prices soon. The hike was likely to spur an all-round increase in prices of goods and commodities in Delhi, besides pushing up transport costs.
The Economic Times
FIRMS SHIFT TO FOREIGN LENDERS

Borrowings from financial institutions (FIs) have become most expensive, with FIs lending at two percent higher than banks and investment institutions. Not surprisingly, corporates are shifting either to foreign lenders as a first option or banks as a second option. The main thrust of the new credit policy, therefore, would be on lowering interest rates and bridging to some extent the gap between international and domestic lending rates.
CURBS ON IMPORT OF CONSUMER GOODS TO GO

Quantative restrictions on the import of consumer goods would be phased out and the sector opened in a few years, the finance secretary said. He said it was logical for companies to increase their competitiveness and face international competition by having mergers, but distinctions should be made between mergers which encouraged competition and mergers which discouraged it.
EXPORT-IMPORT POLICY LIKELY TO HALVE NEGATIVE LIST

The new five-year Export Import policy, effective April 1, 1997, might drastically reduce quantitative restrictions by shifting nearly half the items from the negative list, and incorporating most of the changes sought by industry. Officials said the main objective would be to bring down the number of items in the restricted list in line with the obligations undertaken at the World Trade Organisation. Quantitative restrictions on capital goods would be the first to be removed, followed by raw materials, intermediates and finally consumer goods.
SECRETARIES SUGGEST MORE TEETH FOR BROADCAST LAW

The committee of secretaries recommended many changes to the proposed broadcasting law, including more control over foreign satellite channels. It also suggested working out legalities to allow the government to insist on utilisation of its satellites. The committee also recommended a minimum cap on the number of players for all services and called for more checks on authorised operators.
Financial Express
HINDUSTAN PETROLEUM PREFERS GLOBAL GIANTS

Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) was unlikely to accept the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation's offer to pick up a stake in the former's proposed 55 billion rupee refinery project. Instead, sources said, HPCL would locate another partner for the project, which was initially supposed to be a joint venture with the Oman Oil Company. HPCL would prefer the new partner to be a global oil major and that talks were held with several companies.
100 PCT FOREIGN EQUITY LIKELY IN AIRPORT PROJECTS

The government was likely to approve privatisation of airports and may allow 100 percent foreign equity in airports ventures on a build-operate-transfer basis. However, there would be no change in operation of air traffic services which would continue to be controlled by the Airports Authority of India (AAI).
Business Standard
ICICI PLAN TO MERGE ALL SUBSIDIARIES OVER THREE YEARS

Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) planned to merge all its subsidiaries over the next three years to form a universal bank, its chief executive officer said. Imminent regulatory changes were expected to enable ICICI to knit its subsidiaries into a major financial monolith. Last December, ICICI announced the largest-ever merger in the financial sector with SCICI under a share swap deal to form an entity that could challenge the Industrial Development Bank of India.
IFC STAKE IN INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT CORP RULED OUT

The International Finance Corporation (IFC) was unlikely to participate in the share capital of the Infrastructure Development Finance Corporation (IDFC). Finance Ministry sources said letting the IFC invest in IDFC equity could block the nascent corporation's access to World Bank credit. The ministry expected an infusion of 15 billion rupees in IDFC's share capital from foreign and Indian financial institutions in the next four months.
The Observer
PROMOTERS MAY FIND WAY BARRED

Promoters might be barred from selling their stakes to the company through the proposed buy backs by way of treasury operations facility. This was expected to prevent insider trading by promoters in companies, which planned to go for share buy back. The proposal was now being considered by the department of company affairs. If accepted, the provision would be included in the final version of the Companies Act amendment bill.
APEX BANK ASKED TO TRIM INTEREST RATES

The finance minister urged the central bank to further reduce interest rates and spur bank lending. The minister also asked the RBI to take policy initiatives with a view to containing the annual rate of inflation at 6-7 percent during 1997/98 (April-March). He said though there had been some softening of interest rates since last October, it was not enough and further reduction of lending rates would be desirable and possible.
Business Line
STEPS TO BOOST FUNDS FLOW TO COMMERCIAL SECTOR LIKELY

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) chief hinted at fresh measures in the forthcoming slack season credit policy to boost the flow of bank credit to the commercial sector. Despite successive reductions announced in the cash reserve ratio, actual flow of credit to the corporate sector remained low during the year, the RBI governor pointed out. The monetary policy, he said, would have a two-pronged objective in the future. While one would be to regulate money supply to keep inflationary pressure under control, the second would be to provide adequate credit to bolster economic growth.
